report.source_text: A biochemical work-up for hypoglycaemia revealed non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia with a blood glucose level of 25 mg/dL (normal range: 70-99 mg/dL). Furthermore, there were concomitant low serum insulin levels (1 microIU/mL, normal range: 6-27 microIU/mL), low serum C-peptide levels (<0.5 microg/L, normal range: 0.5-4.0 microg/L), and low serum IGF-1 levels for sex and age (60 mcg/L, below the 1st percentile). The pituitary function was found to be normal, and cortisol deficiency was ruled out. Additionally, insulin antibodies tested negative. The renal and hepatic functions were within normal limits. A complete blood count and metabolic panel excluded anemia and electrolyte imbalances (Table 2).

report.source_text: A continuous infusion of 10% glucose was promptly administered, and the patient was advised to have frequent meals. However, episodes of hypoglycemia continued to occur. Due to the recurrence of symptoms, the medical team proposed a surgical approach. Consequently, the patient underwent a right posterolateral open thoracotomy for mass resection. The tumor, originating from the anterior mediastinum, was located within the right lung. A portion of the lower lobe of the right lung was resected. The encapsulated mass measured 25.3×19×17 cm and weighed 3720 g (Fig. 4).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Doege-Potter syndrome (non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia associated with solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of recurrent severe fasting hypoglycemia (blood glucose 20-50 mg/dL) accompanied by adrenergic symptoms (excessive sweating, tremors, weakness) and dyspnea. Biochemical workup revealed non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia with suppressed insulin (1 microIU/mL), low C-peptide (<0.5 microg/L), and markedly low IGF-1 (60 mcg/L, <1st percentile), consistent with non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH). Imaging studies (chest X-ray, CT, and echocardiography) identified a large heterogeneous pleural mass (22.5×16.5×22.5 cm) in the right lower hemithorax compressing the right atrium. Pathological examination of a biopsy specimen confirmed solitary fibrous tumor (SFT) with characteristic immunophenotype: CD34+, STAT6+, Bcl-2+, spindle-shaped cells without necrosis, and negative staining for S100, CK7, WT1, D2-40, calretinin, and MDM2. Initial conservative management with continuous glucose infusion and frequent meals failed to control hypoglycemia. The patient underwent right posterolateral thoracotomy with resection of the encapsulated mass (25.3×19×17 cm, 3720 g) from the anterior mediastinum within the right lung, including partial lower lobe resection. Surgical specimen histology confirmed SFT. Post-operatively, serum glucose levels normalized, hypoglycemic episodes resolved, dyspnea completely resolved, and the patient was discharged without recurrent hypoglycemia. Follow-up chest radiograph at 2 weeks showed pulmonary re-expansion in the right hemithorax.
